title: Bambusa vulgaris leaves reverse mitochondria dysfunction in diabetic rats through modulation of mitochondria biogenic genes.
authors: Elekofehinti, Olusola Olalekan; Aladenika, Yetunde Victoria; Iwaloye, Opeyemi; Okon, Enoabasi Ima-Abasi; Adanlawo, Isaac Gbadura
journal: Hormone molecular biology and clinical investigation
one_liner_zh: 该文研究竹叶提取物对糖尿病大鼠线粒体生物发生基因的调控作用，仅涉及基因表达和分子对接，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: OBJECTIVES: There is evidence that mitochondrial dysfunction mediated by hyperglycemia increases the incidence of diabetes and age-related insulin resistance. Thus, maintaining mitochondrial integrity may provide alternative therapeutic approach in diabetes treatment. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of Bambusa vulgaris leaf extract on mitochondrial biogenesis in the pancreas of diabetic rats. METHODS: 11 weeks old male rats (n=30) were purchased, and sorted into the following groups: control, diabetic control, diabetes + metformin (100 mg/kg), diabetes + Aq. B. vulgaris (100 mg/kg), diabetes + Aq. B. vulgaris (200 mg/kg), and diabetes + Aq. B. vulgaris (300 mg/kg). Diabetes was induced in the rats by a single dose of 65 mg/kg streptozotocin (STZ). The mRNA expression of genes related to mitochondria biogenesis (pgc-1alpha, Nrf2, GSK3beta, AMPK and SIRT2) and genes of Nrf2-Keap1-ARE signaling pathway were determined by reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction. Molecular docking studies including lock and key docking and prime MM-GBSA were incorporated to identify the lead chemical compounds in Bambusa vulgari. RESULTS: The results showed that B. vulgaris leaf extract promotes mitochondrial biogenesis via altering the mRNA expression of mitochondrial master regulator pgc-1alpha, other upstream genes, and the Nrf2-Keap1-ARE antioxidant pathway. Through molecular docking results, cryptochlorogenic acid, hesperidin, orientin, vitexin, scopolin, and neochlorogenic were found as the crucial chemicals in B. vulgaris with the most modulating effect on PGC-1alpha, AMPK, and GSK3. CONCLUSIONS: This study thus suggests that B. vulgaris leaf extract restores the integrity of mitochondria in diabetic rats.
abstract_zh: 目的：有证据表明，由高血糖介导的线粒体功能障碍会增加糖尿病及年龄相关胰岛素抵抗的发生率。因此，维持线粒体完整性可能为糖尿病治疗提供替代性方法。本研究旨在评估竹叶提取物对糖尿病大鼠胰腺线粒体生物发生的影响。方法：购买11周龄雄性大鼠（n=30），并分为以下组别：对照组、糖尿病对照组、糖尿病+二甲双胍（100 mg/kg）、糖尿病+竹叶水提物（100 mg/kg）、糖尿病+竹叶水提物（200 mg/kg）和糖尿病+竹叶水提物（300 mg/kg）。通过单次注射65 mg/kg链脲佐菌素（STZ）诱导大鼠糖尿病。采用逆转录聚合酶链反应测定与线粒体生物发生相关基因（pgc-1alpha、Nrf2、GSK3beta、AMPK和SIRT2）及Nrf2-Keap1-ARE信号通路基因的mRNA表达。结合锁钥对接和prime MM-GBSA的分子对接研究用于鉴定竹叶中的主要化学化合物。结果：结果表明，竹叶提取物通过改变线粒体主调控因子pgc-1alpha、其他上游基因及Nrf2-Keap1-ARE抗氧化通路的mRNA表达，促进线粒体生物发生。通过分子对接结果，隐绿原酸、橙皮苷、荭草苷、牡荆素、东莨菪苷和新绿原酸被鉴定为竹叶中对PGC-1alpha、AMPK和GSK3具有最显著调节作用的关键化学物质。结论：因此，本研究提示竹叶提取物可恢复糖尿病大鼠的线粒体完整性。
